items.body:
## Summary

The MCP setup documentation and configuration reference advertise `experimental_environment = "remote"` for remote stdio MCP servers. The stable CLI rejects this field during strict configuration loading, before it can initialize the server. This is incorrect documentation with a consequential setup failure. The supported `environment_id` field provides a working alternative.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the installed stable CLI identified under Runtime or environment. No account, model request, MCP connection, or registered executor is required to reproduce the configuration rejection.

1. Create an isolated configuration containing the documented field and invoke strict configuration loading:

```sh
probe_home=$(mktemp -d)
cat > "$probe_home/config.toml" <<'TOML'
[mcp_servers.env_probe]
command = "/usr/bin/python3"
args = ["-c", "pass"]
experimental_environment = "remote"
TOML
HOME="$probe_home" CODEX_HOME="$probe_home" CODEX_EXEC_SERVER_URL=none \
  codex app-server --stdio --strict-config < /dev/null
```

2. Observe the unknown-field error and exit status 1. The command and arguments are a disposable parser fixture, not an MCP implementation.
3. As a parsing control, replace the documented field with `environment_id = "staging"`, initialize the app-server connection, and request `config/read`. The effective MCP configuration includes that environment ID. This control checks configuration syntax only and does not connect to an executor named `staging`.

## Expected behavior

The official remote stdio MCP setup instructions should identify the field and value accepted by the applicable CLI configuration schema, so following them passes strict configuration validation. They should explain how the value identifies the intended registered executor.

## Actual behavior

The first step exits with status 1 and reports:

```text
unknown configuration field `mcp_servers.env_probe.experimental_environment`
```

The reduced four-line configuration reproduces the same rejection as the remote integration fixture. Replacing the field with `environment_id` passes strict loading and returns that field through `config/read`. In a separate executed control, an owned loopback executor registered as `remote-probe` initialized a stdio MCP fixture configured with `environment_id = "remote-probe"`, discovered its tool, and completed a tool call. That integration control used macOS on both ends.

## Evidence

- Expected source: The official [MCP documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp.md), lines 154 and 155, lists `experimental_environment` and says to set it to `remote`; the [configuration reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference.md), entry `mcp_servers.<id>.experimental_environment`, also lists the field. Both pages still contain it when checked for this report.
- Failure source: Executed isolated `app-server --stdio --strict-config` invocation with the four-line TOML above returned the quoted error and exit status 1.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The [release configuration type](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d27764b82f7118f674371e6d6e76271d9d606edb/codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs#L401) accepts `environment_id`. The [current main configuration schema](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0b863c69f50335acd92164aab971cb58d298c2fe/codex-rs/core/config.schema.json#L3778) also exposes that field. Neither checked schema contains `experimental_environment`. The main source was inspected, not compiled or executed.

## Restoration check

Following the corrected remote stdio MCP guidance should pass strict configuration loading on the supported CLI version and resolve to the intended registered executor. Keep the unknown-field rejection as a discriminating control so success cannot come from disabling strict validation. An MCP fixture on the registered executor should initialize, expose a tool, and complete a bounded tool call using the documented configuration.

## Runtime or environment

- Executed CLI: `codex-cli 0.160.1`, user-local npm package, native macOS 27.0 arm64.
- Latest published stable release at verification: [`rust-v0.160.1`](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.160.1), with `prerelease: false`.
- Source baselines: the pinned release configuration type and current `main` schema linked in Evidence. Source inspection agrees with the runtime parsing result; no claim is made about executing a main build or native Windows behavior.
- All runtime probes used disposable configuration directories. No live configuration was changed, no model turn was sent, and the owned app-server and executor processes exited after the probes.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: Following the documented field blocks strict remote MCP configuration startup. The failure is bounded to configurations using that field and has an observed safe alternative.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: `environment_id` passes strict configuration loading, and setting it to the owned executor's registered ID allowed an MCP fixture to initialize and complete a tool call without weakening validation.

# Desktop regression: existing local chats intermittently disappear from project sidebar

## Environment

- macOS; ChatGPT desktop app with local Codex chats
- Installed desktop version: 26.930.61225, build 13232
- Observed on 2026-10-06
- Project grouping on the Work surface; chats sorted by updated time
- Existing ChatGPT-backed projects represented by legacy `g-p-*` project IDs

## Actual behavior

After a desktop update, multiple existing local chats disappeared from their expanded project groups. The issue affected at least two projects. An expanded project displayed only three chats and no load-more control, although 17 active local chats were recorded with that project's legacy assignment.

The chats remained readable through direct thread access and were not archived. This appears to affect discovery/project display rather than confirmed loss of conversation content.

The problem recurred during the investigation. After supported sidebar operations and catalog reads, the user reported that the project chats were visible again. A reliable single-action workaround or deterministic reproduction has not been established.

## Concrete evidence

1. For two sampled chats, the supported `list_threads` response returned `projectId: null` while the local `thread-project-assignments` setting still contained an explicit local project assignment for the same thread. One sample belonged to each affected project.
2. `local_thread_catalog.project_id` was NULL for both sampled chats. NULL catalog project IDs also occur for visible chats, so this is diagnostic context, not independent proof of the root cause.
3. Local settings recorded `projectsMigrated: true` and `threadAssignmentsMigrated: false` with pending thread assignments. The installed code gates assignment migration on a feature flag, so an incomplete flag alone must not be treated as a proven failed migration.
4. Startup logs on the same day contained:

   ```text
   2026-10-06T05:22:15.990Z info [host-app-server-projects] Local app-server project migration completed projectCount=17
   2026-10-06T05:24:14.223Z info [host-app-server-projects] Local app-server project migration completed projectCount=17
   ```

5. As a separate observation, five chats were pinned through the supported API and confirmed in a following read. A later read returned the original ten pins without those five. Re-pinning them and reading back restored the five. This may be a related state persistence issue, but the user's main issue is project groups, not pinned chats.

## Expected behavior

All non-archived local chats explicitly assigned to a project remain discoverable in that project's sidebar group across updates and normal navigation. If pagination is required, the group exposes a working load-more control. Supported operations and subsequent catalog reads agree on project membership.

## Investigation steps / reproduction guidance

1. Use an upgraded desktop profile with existing ChatGPT-backed project IDs and local chats explicitly assigned through legacy settings.
2. Expand an affected project group and compare displayed entries with active saved assignments. Do not assume absence means archiving.
3. Compare `list_threads.projectId`, legacy `thread-project-assignments`, native thread/project metadata and catalog membership for the same chats.
4. Check whether membership resolution changes after normal navigation or a supported sidebar state write. In this incident, several interventions preceded recovery, so the precise trigger is unknown.
5. Verify that pin and membership state survive subsequent reads and normal application activity.

## Suspected area, not proven root cause

Project-membership resolution, migration or state invalidation between legacy assignments, the local catalog and the sidebar's combined project sources. Investigate why an explicit saved assignment can resolve to `null` and why a project scope can show a partial list without a load-more control.

No internal databases or migration flags were edited, no chats were deleted, and no conversations were sent new prompts as part of diagnosis. Read-only database/settings inspections and supported app operations were used. Project grouping was toggled, existing chats were opened and pins were changed; these actions prevent attributing recovery to a single operation.

## Related reports

- #51369: entire ChatGPT projects missing on the same desktop version/build.
- #51041: sidebar entries return after switching surfaces on Windows.
- #49121: ChatGPT project sidebar recovery/state inconsistency on macOS.

This incident concerns missing chats inside project groups that remain visible, plus a mismatch between explicit saved membership and API output. Shared root cause is unconfirmed.

Submitted by an AI assistant at the user's explicit request. This public report omits private chat contents, project names, identifiers and paths.


## Follow-up: third affected project

The user also reported many missing chats inside a third project group. Read-only inspection found 25 active local chats with explicit saved membership in this third project. The full sidebar visibility was not independently measurable through the available API, whose non-pinned result limit is 50 globally. All 25 were navigated to through the supported app interface to refresh access; this does not establish a durable sidebar repair. This extends the reported scope beyond the first two projects. Private names, chat titles and identifiers remain omitted.

items.title: Windows sandbox keeps locking itself out of `.sandbox-bin` — finally found why (and a fix that actually sticks)
items.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?
Desktop 26.930.7945.0 from the Store, engine 0.160.1. Windows 11 Pro 26300. Plus plan.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?
Honestly, just use it the way I do: a ChatGPT Work thread that runs on my PC plus some local tasks, switching back and forth during the day. Within a day or two every command starts failing with

```
Failed to create unified exec process: exec-server rejected request (-32603): sandbox provisioning failed
```

and attachments die with

```
cannot create attachment directory: failed to prepare fs sandbox: failed to prepare windows sandbox wrapper: sandbox provisioning failed
```

Clicking the "update sandbox" UAC prompt brings it back for a while, then it dies again. I reinstalled Windows over this. Didn't help — same thing again two days after a clean install.

## What do you see instead?
After three days of this I started reading the logs in `.codex\.sandbox` and then the actual source for 0.160.1. This is what's going on:

- The folder `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox-bin` gets created by **my** user process before the service is ever called (`gather_helper_read_roots()` does a `create_dir_all`, and that runs inside `require_logon_sandbox_creds()` before `require_sandbox_account()`). So I own it.
- The first time the service provisions, it works — the folder still inherits SYSTEM Full Control from my profile. Then `lock_sandbox_bin_dir()` slaps a **protected** DACL on it: SYSTEM `0x1301bf`, Administrators `0x1301bf`, me `0x1701bf`, CodexSandboxUsers `0x1200a9`. Notice neither SYSTEM nor Administrators gets `WRITE_DAC`.
- Next time the service needs to provision again, it opens that same folder with `READ_CONTROL | WRITE_DAC` (`lock_sandbox_dir`, the ProvisionOnly branch). It's running as LocalSystem, it isn't the owner, it has no WRITE_DAC, inheritance is blocked. Open fails. Log says:

```
setup error: helper_sandbox_lock_failed: lock sandbox bin dir \\?\C:\Users\<user>\.codex\.sandbox-bin failed: open directory \\?\C:\Users\<user>\.codex\.sandbox-bin
```

  and nothing else, because the real error gets dropped on the way out (`{err}` only prints the outer context). Took me a while to figure out it was an access denied.

- Worst part: `prepare_setup_marker()` deletes `setup_marker.json` **before** provisioning. So when provisioning fails, the marker is a 0-byte file and from then on every single command says `sandbox setup marker missing or incompatible` → calls the service → fails again. Everything is bricked until I click the UAC setup, which works because that one runs as *me* (the owner). But the UAC setup stores `proxy_ports=[]`, and my cloud-connected Work thread wants `[3128, 8081]`, so the very next command from that thread triggers `offline firewall settings changed` → service → dead again. That's the whole "intermittent" thing. I counted: every one of the 6 "settings changed" events in my logs was followed by a failed provisioning.

- I also tried what people suggested in the other issues — adding a SYSTEM WRITE_DAC ACE by hand. It worked for exactly one provisioning and then vanished, because `lock_sandbox_bin_dir()` is also called from the per-command refresh (`run_setup_full`) and rewrites the whole DACL every time. Watched it happen: ACE added 18:13:25, one successful provisioning 18:15:19, ACE gone, failure at 18:15:24.

Numbers from my `sandbox-*.log` files before the fix: 17 service provisioning attempts over 3 days, 15 failed, 2 succeeded (the very first one after install, and the two minutes the hand-added ACE existed).

## What fixed it
One command, as admin:

```
takeown /F "%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox-bin" /A
```

Owner becomes `BUILTIN\Administrators`. LocalSystem has Administrators in its token, so it gets implicit READ_CONTROL/WRITE_DAC as owner. I didn't touch the DACL at all (backed up the SDDL first). This sticks because Codex only ever rewrites the DACL — never the owner.

Since then: 4 full re-provisionings (3 of them were the normal settings flips in both directions while I just used the thing) — **4 for 4**, zero lock failures, 59 sandboxed commands, `setup_error.json` gone, and the attachment download that started all this works again in the same thread. Someone in #50520 did basically the same owner change and reports it survived a reboot and a desktop update too.

Why the other workarounds don't last: renaming/recreating `.sandbox-bin` (#45734, #46380) only buys you one provisioning — my user process recreates it user-owned and the service locks itself out again on the next round. `icacls /setowner "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM"` fails with error 5 (needs SeRestorePrivilege); `takeown /A` doesn't need that.

## What is the expected behavior?
Re-provisioning should just work. Or at the very least, failing to provision shouldn't nuke the previous working setup.

## Additional information
If it helps, the fix on your side looks small:
1. Give SYSTEM (or Administrators) `WRITE_DAC` in that DACL, or have the service take ownership of `.sandbox-bin` before locking it.
2. Don't delete `setup_marker.json` until the new provisioning actually succeeded.
3. Put the real `io::Error` in the `helper_sandbox_lock_failed` message so the next person doesn't have to guess.

Checked `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/{setup.rs, identity.rs, setup_provisioning.rs, no_reparse_dir.rs, setup_provisioning/sandbox_users.rs}` and `windows-sandbox-service/src/provisioning.rs` at `rust-v0.160.1`; same code on `main` as of Oct 6.

Same symptom reports: #50520 #46380 #36475 #45734 #45153 #49025 #51111. Please don't close this as a duplicate — those describe the symptom, this one is the cause.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

- Codex App 26.930.41038 (published Oct 3, 2026) - Codex App 26.930.61225 (published Oct 5, 2026)  Also tested an older rollback build (26.818.61809) with the same Remote SSH timeout.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19042.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

Codex Desktop fails to connect to a Debian VPS over Remote SSH with:

`SSH: codex path probe timed out after 60000ms`

However, the SSH connection itself works correctly, authentication succeeds, `command -v codex` works remotely, and even the exact remote probe command generated by Codex Desktop succeeds immediately when executed outside the app.

This strongly suggests an issue in Codex Desktop's handling of the SSH probe process/output rather than a server-side SSH or PATH problem.

## Environment

Local machine:
- Windows x64
- Codex Desktop
- OpenSSH_for_Windows_7.7p1
- SSH key: ED25519
- SSH agent enabled

Remote machine:
- Debian 12
- OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u10
- Shell: `/bin/bash`
- Node.js: `v22.23.1`
- npm: `10.9.8`
- Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.160.1`
- Codex path: `/usr/bin/codex`

Codex Desktop transport:
- `ssh-websocket-v0`

Failure stage seen in Codex Desktop logs:
- `sshSetupStage=remote_codex_lookup`
- `SSH: codex path probe timed out after 60000ms`

## SSH configuration

The host is configured through `~/.ssh/config` with an SSH alias. The key is loaded in the Windows SSH agent. A normal SSH connection works without prompting for the key passphrase.

## What works

### 1. Normal SSH connection

```powershell
ssh hyperpbx
```

Works correctly.

### 2. Non-interactive Codex lookup

```powershell
ssh -T hyperpbx "command -v codex"
```

Result:

```text
/usr/bin/codex
```

### 3. Login + interactive shell lookup

```powershell
ssh -o BatchMode=yes hyperpbx "timeout 10s /bin/bash -l -i -c 'command -v codex'"
```

Result:

```text
bash: cannot set terminal process group (...): Inappropriate ioctl for device
bash: no job control in this shell
/usr/bin/codex
```

The command exits normally.

### 4. SSH exec channel

```powershell
ssh -v -o BatchMode=yes hyperpbx "sh -c 'printf CODEX_PROBE_OK; command -v codex; exit 0'"
```

Result:

```text
Authentication succeeded (publickey).
Sending command: sh -c 'printf CODEX_PROBE_OK; command -v codex; exit 0'
CODEX_PROBE_OK/usr/bin/codex
Exit status 0
```

### 5. Exact Codex Desktop path probe

While Codex Desktop was attempting the connection, I captured the exact `ssh.exe` command line using:

```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process |
    Where-Object { $_.Name -eq "ssh.exe" } |
    Select-Object ProcessId,ParentProcessId,CommandLine |
    Format-List
```

Codex Desktop launches SSH using:

```text
-v
-o BatchMode=yes
-o ServerAliveInterval=15
-o ServerAliveCountMax=12
```

The remote shell wrapper checks `$SHELL`, sets `CODEX_REMOTE_PAYLOAD`, starts the login shell with `-l -i`, sets `CODEX_HOME`, adjusts `PATH`, checks `command -v codex`, and emits an 8-byte probe marker.

I reproduced this exact probe outside Codex Desktop using Python `subprocess.run()` so that PowerShell quoting would not modify the command.

Result:

```text
RETURN CODE: 0
STDOUT RAW: b'\xb0\x9e\xf7)\xde\xc7\xf2\xb0'
```

SSH debug output also shows:

```text
Authentication succeeded (publickey).
Sending command: ...
Exit status 0
```

The complete probe finishes in approximately 0.2 seconds.

## Server-side confirmation

While Codex Desktop is trying to connect, the Debian SSH logs show successful public-key authentication:

```text
Accepted publickey for <user> from <client-ip> ...
pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user <user>
```

Multiple SSH sessions are opened successfully. SFTP sessions also start correctly. A separate `sshd: <user>@notty` session remains open during the Codex path probe attempt and eventually corresponds to the 60-second timeout.

## Codex Desktop behavior

Despite the exact same probe succeeding outside Codex Desktop, the app waits approximately 60 seconds and then reports:

```text
SSH: codex path probe timed out after 60000ms
```

The app then retries and repeats the same behavior.

## Troubleshooting already performed

- Verified SSH authentication
- Verified SSH agent
- Verified BatchMode
- Verified remote exec channel
- Verified remote shell
- Verified login + interactive shell behavior
- Verified PATH
- Verified `/usr/bin/codex`
- Verified Codex CLI version
- Verified exact Codex-generated probe
- Verified binary probe marker output
- Verified clean SSH process state before retry
- Reset Codex Desktop local state
- Tested more than one Codex Desktop version
- Same timeout remains

## Expected behavior

Codex Desktop should detect the successful remote probe and continue with remote app-server setup.

## Actual behavior

The remote probe succeeds at the SSH/process level but Codex Desktop does not detect completion and waits until:

`codex path probe timed out after 60000ms`

## Suspected area

Possibly in the Windows Desktop handling of:
- spawned `ssh.exe` process lifecycle
- stdout/stderr handling
- binary probe marker detection
- EOF / process completion detection
- `ssh-websocket-v0` remote setup logic

The SSH server itself appears to behave correctly.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows, configure a working SSH alias for a Debian 12 host in `~/.ssh/config` and load the ED25519 key into the Windows SSH agent.
2. Verify that the host works from PowerShell:

```powershell
ssh hyperpbx
ssh -T hyperpbx "command -v codex"
```

The second command returns `/usr/bin/codex`.

3. In Codex Desktop, go to Settings > Connections > SSH and enable the discovered `hyperpbx` connection.
4. Codex Desktop opens successful SSH sessions on the server, but the connection remains on "Connecting".
5. After approximately 60 seconds, Codex Desktop reports:

```text
SSH: codex path probe timed out after 60000ms
```

6. Capture the exact `ssh.exe` command generated by Codex Desktop with:

```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process |
    Where-Object { $_.Name -eq "ssh.exe" } |
    Select-Object ProcessId,ParentProcessId,CommandLine |
    Format-List
```

7. Re-run the exact remote path probe outside Codex Desktop using Python `subprocess.run()` to preserve quoting. The probe completes in about 0.2 seconds with exit code 0 and returns the expected 8-byte binary marker.

No session ID, token limit, or context-window usage is applicable because the failure happens during Remote SSH setup before a Codex session is established.


### What is the expected behavior?

Codex Desktop should recognize that the remote Codex path probe completed successfully, detect `/usr/bin/codex`, and continue with the Remote SSH app-server setup instead of waiting for the 60-second timeout.

### Additional information

The same failure persists after resetting Codex Desktop local state and after testing more than one Codex Desktop version.

The server-side `sshd` logs confirm successful public-key authentication and session creation during each Codex Desktop attempt. Manual SSH, SFTP, non-interactive exec, login/interactive shell execution, and the exact Codex-generated path probe all work correctly outside Codex Desktop.

For privacy, public IP addresses, the local Windows username, and the remote username can be redacted in any attached logs.

The application treated that process as another active dictation instance and blocked shortcut registration.

Backing up and moving only the confirmed abandoned ownership lock restored dictation. The user verified that dictation worked afterward. No application code was modified.

## Affected version

Windows desktop package `26.930.7945.0`. Version obtained from installed package information.

## Reproduction status

One diagnosed incident with verified recovery. The event that abandoned the lock has not been established.

Suggested maintainer regression: in an isolated fixture, create a valid ownership record for an exited app process, make process inspection resolve the same numeric PID to a different live process, then attempt dictation activation. The stale owner should be reclaimed. This fixture has not been run against an instrumented desktop build.

## Expected behavior and suggested fix

Validate durable process identity, such as PID plus process creation time, before treating an ownership record as live. Recover stale ownership atomically while preserving a genuinely active owner.

Acceptance checks:
- Reused PID: dictation can activate.
- Genuine active owner: a second instance cannot take ownership.
- Concurrent stale-owner recovery: exactly one owner.
- Failed shortcut registration: show an actionable error in Settings.

## Classification and related reports

Observed impact: local dictation availability. No demonstrated security exploit; no security severity claimed.

Related symptom: #46452. Its report does not establish stale-owner PID reuse. Public issue searches found no exact root-cause match; differently worded/private reports may exist.

Prepared with AI assistance at the user's request. This report contains no local paths, PID values, timestamps, log extracts, account identifiers, or private conversation content.

Automatic discovery reports: “Couldn't discover OAuth settings. Check the server URL or enter settings manually.” After entering the OAuth configuration manually, clicking Create reports: “Couldn't create MCP app, try again.” ### Steps 1. Run a temporary Go MCP server exposed over HTTPS through Tailscale Funnel. 2. In the macOS app, open Plugins → Add → Create MCP app, enter the HTTPS MCP URL and select OAuth. 3. After discovery fails, enter the authorization-server base, authorization URL, token URL, resource URL, scope and pre-registered public client ID. Use the exact callback shown in the UI, no client secret, token endpoint auth method None, and OpenID disabled. Leave Registration URL empty for the pre-registered client. 4. Click Create. Creation fails without opening the OAuth login page. ### Checks performed Observed on October 6, 2026, around 1:48–2:06 p.m. America/Toronto. During the active test, external probes returned 401 with an authentication challenge at the MCP endpoint and 200 for OAuth metadata. Server access logs contained no requests corresponding to the failed creation attempts. Reviewing 4,775 lines of desktop app logs did not identify a creation error or request ID. We compared the complete UI configuration with the server configuration and found no mismatch. These checks do not establish the root cause. The temporary server is now shut down. ### Expected behavior Create the custom MCP app and open its OAuth authorization flow, or return an actionable validation/connection error with a request ID. ### Feedback reference Feedback ID: 01a11145-a9aa-7588-beeb-919e3d7fa034 Please correlate the submitted desktop feedback/diagnostics and route this report to the appropriate component if custom MCP app creation is handled outside this repository. ### Subscription Not provided in this report. ### Sanitized Go diagnostic specimen The following source and README are a sanitized diagnostic specimen, compiled with Go 1.26.1 but not executed in sanitized form. This is not a confirmed minimal reproduction. Personal endpoints and identifiers were replaced by explicit configuration; automatic tunnel management was removed. The temporary login form is served by the operator's configured SPIKE_ORIGIN, not by ChatGPT itself.

items.body: ### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? 26.930.61225 ### What subscription do you have? Pro(5x) ### What platform is your computer? Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm ### What issue are you seeing? ### Description There is a typo in the Turkish localization of the unified ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on macOS. In the ChatGPT application menu, the "Check for Updates..." item is currently translated as: "Güncellemeleri Genetle..." This is incorrect Turkish. It should be: "Güncellemeleri denetle..." ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on macOS. 2. Use the Turkish interface. 3. Open the "ChatGPT" menu in the macOS menu bar. 4. Observe the "Güncellemeleri Genetle..." menu item. ### Actual behavior "Güncellemeleri Genetle..." ### Expected behavior "Güncellemeleri denetle..." ### Environment - Product: Unified ChatGPT/Codex desktop app - Operating system: macOS - Interface language: Turkish - App version: 26.930.61225 ### Additional context Screenshot attached. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Open the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on macOS with the interface language set to Turkish. 2. Click "ChatGPT" in the macOS menu bar. 3. Look at the menu item for checking application updates. 4. The item is displayed as "Güncellemeleri Genetle...". The typo is consistently visible whenever this menu is opened. ### What is the expected behavior? The menu item should be displayed as: "Güncellemeleri denetle..." instead of: "Güncellemeleri Genetle..." "Genetle" is not the correct Turkish word here. "Denetle" is the correct translation for "Check" in the context of "Check for Updates". ### Additional information This appears to be a Turkish localization/translation typo rather than a functional issue. The issue is present in: - Codex App version: 26.930.61225 - Platform: macOS / Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 A screenshot showing the incorrect menu text is attached.
